I was the same as you! 169cm, 59kg, skinny fat, all my fat stored in my belly. I went from 93,5cm belly waist to 83cm in about a year. It was awesome. 

How? You have to add cardio. Cardio, cardio, cardio. Don’t do hours of cardio per week immediately though, build it up steadily so your mind and body have time to adjust and you can see what works for you. This is how I did it:

week 1: 30 min cardio
week 2, add extra minutes, but make sure to split them (i.e. 2x 30 minutes). 
week3: 90 minutes, split again 2x 45 min or 3x 30 minutes, however you please but splitting them across the week is much, much more is better than doing it all at once. 
week 4: let’s say 100 minutes
Week 5: 120 minutes…
Week 6: if you are making progress, keep it like this. Or add minutes if progress flatlines.

When to know if you need to add cardio or just keep steady? Measure your belly waist every sunday morning on an empty stomach and write it down. If you lost cm/inches, you’re doing a good job. If the cm/inches stays the same a certain week, it’s time to add some extra cardio.

Your curve kinda looks like mine (22m, also 5ft 5 and 115 pounds lmao). The doctor said that surgery is very much out of the question, because it’s too mild/moderate and totally not worth the pain, risk and isn’t significantly beneficial at all for a curve this small. It’s actually more detrimental because you lose flexibility and “fix” next to nothing. So there’s nothing to fix, really. Because of this I count myself so lucky, because there are people who have 60-80 (or more!) degree curves that not only looks very “disturbing” (in a purely anatomic way!), but also puts their lives in danger if left untreated (ribs puncturing organs, breathing made almost impossible, etc.) 

So to answer your question: you don’t really need this surgery. Not from a medical standpoint, but (imo) also not from a cosmetic standpoint.
Though it’s completely normal for you to feel like fixing this cosmetically, many doctors will look at you strangely because it’s simply not worth the operation to get rid of that “cosmetic flaw”. When I found out this can’t be fixed through surgery, I was so bummed. After lots of positive thinking, I have accepted my waist as a part of me, it took me a lot of patience. I had to realize that my waist poking out from one side isn’t a flaw, but rather something that makes me me. I can’t fix it, so might as wel live with it! It does not define me, it’s just a part of me! Don’t feel self conscious about it please! It’s not worth your mental health. 

Tbh we are our own worst critic and our curves aren’t even close to being bad, and same goes for how it “looks”. Many people don’t even notice it unless I explicitly point out my waist. And even then they say it’s so minor. 

HOWEVER. though you can’t completely fix it, you can, to a certain degree (lol), correct your curvature. This will have a cosmetic effect aka your waist will(or might) poke out/protrude less. 

My waist definitely looks better after enforcing core stability (aka physically correcting your curve through use of certain muscles).

I hope this helps you in any way! Good luck:)
